title: state
notes: Persistent lexical variables; initialization runs once.

title: say
notes: Prints its arguments with an appended newline.

title: defined-or
notes: // selects the fallback only for undef; zero and empty strings are defined.

title: subroutine signatures
notes: Positional parameters with arity checks; stable since 5.36, not named parameters.

title: postfix dereferencing
notes: Postfix ->@* and ->%* dereference collections; stable since 5.24.

title: postfix dereferencing in strings
notes: Enables interpolated postfix dereferences; stable since 5.24. Ordinary ->{key} needs no new pragma.

title: unicode_strings
notes: Uses Unicode string semantics; does not decode input or enable UTF-8 source.

title: try/catch exception handling
notes: Catch exceptions with try and catch; the catch variable is a bare lexical variable, not my $e. Do not use finally, which remains experimental.

title: multi-variable foreach loops
notes: A for my ($key, $value) (...) loop consumes successive pairs. Use a deterministic even-length list; do not combine with experimental reference aliases.

title: defined-or and logical-or signature defaults
notes: Signature defaults using $value //= EXPR or $value ||= EXPR also handle supplied undef or false values respectively; ordinary = defaults apply only when an argument is omitted.

title: high-precedence logical xor
notes: ^^ tests whether exactly one operand is true. It is logical, not bitwise ^, and unlike && and || must evaluate both operands.

title: logical xor assignment
notes: ^^= assigns the logical exclusive-or result back to its left operand. Distinguish truth-value toggling from numeric bitwise ^=.

title: explicit source encoding
notes: source::encoding accepts ascii or utf8, checking source text rather than decoding external input. The utf8 form is equivalent to use utf8. Use the actual module name source::encoding. Put the encoding pragma on its own line before the first line containing non-ASCII source.

title: lexical method invocation
notes: The ->& syntax invokes a lexical subroutine with the invocant as its first argument, bypassing name-based method resolution. Use my sub and an ordinary blessed package; do not use experimental class syntax.

title: builtin trim
notes: trim returns a string without leading or trailing whitespace; the original is unchanged. Internal whitespace remains.

title: builtin indexed
notes: indexed returns alternating zero-based indices and copied values in list context. Do not call it in scalar context.

title: builtin true and false
notes: true and false provide boolean values, not strings. Do not use experimental is_bool to demonstrate them.

title: builtin weak-reference utilities
notes: weaken, unweaken and is_weak control reference strength. A weak reference becomes undef when no strong reference remains.

title: builtin refaddr
notes: refaddr identifies a referent. Compare addresses for equality; never print addresses because their values vary between runs.

title: builtin reftype and blessed
notes: reftype reports the underlying container type; blessed reports an object class or undef. Avoid printing undef without a fallback.

title: builtin ceil and floor
notes: ceil rounds toward positive infinity and floor toward negative infinity. Use finite, exactly representable example inputs.

title: Unicode 17 character properties
notes: Perl 5.44 supports Unicode 17. Sidetic is a new script in U+10940..U+1095F. Demonstrate chr(0x10940) and \p{Script=Sidetic}; print boolean results rather than relying on font support.

title: regular expression set operations
notes: Extended bracketed classes (?[ ... ]) combine character sets with intersection, subtraction and union. They became stable in 5.36; use literal sets and deterministic examples.

title: noncapturing variable-length lookbehind
notes: Variable-length lookbehind without capturing parentheses is stable in 5.36. Use bounded lengths and avoid captures inside the lookbehind, which remain experimental.

title: regular expression script runs
notes: (*script_run:...) constrains a match to a compatible Unicode script run. Demonstrate fixed Latin and Cyrillic text; this is not a complete spoofing defence.

title: chained comparisons
notes: Compatible comparisons of the same precedence can chain, as in 0 <= $value < 10. Do not mix precedence groups or treat arbitrary operators as chainable.

title: explicit octal literals
notes: 0o prefixes make octal literals explicit; oct also accepts that prefix. Demonstrate conversion with fixed numeric values without changing real file permissions.

title: whitespace inside braced regex constructs
notes: Blanks beside braces and around a quantifier comma are permitted, as in a{ 2, 4 }, even without /x. Do not insert spaces inside numeric digits.

title: indented here-documents
notes: <<~ permits an indented closing delimiter and strips its matching leading whitespace from every content line. Lines must have the required indentation.

title: the capture array
notes: @{^CAPTURE} contains captures from the last successful match; index zero corresponds to $1. Copy results before another match changes them.

title: key/value hash slices
notes: %hash{LIST} returns alternating keys and values. Use a fixed key list to control output order; distinguish it from the value-only @hash{LIST} slice.

title: index/value array slices
notes: %array[LIST] returns alternating indices and values for selected array elements. The percent sigil does not turn the source array into a hash.

title: deleting key/value hash slices
notes: delete %hash{LIST} removes selected entries and returns their keys and old values. Use an explicit key order and inspect the remaining hash deterministically.

title: initializing persistent arrays and hashes
notes: state @items = (...) and state %counts = (...) support one-time aggregate initialization. This does not permit initializing a list of state variables.

title: Unicode word boundaries
notes: \b{wb} follows Unicode word-boundary rules, including apostrophes within words. It differs from ordinary \b and is not a complete language-aware tokenizer.

title: Unicode line-break opportunities
notes: \b{lb} matches Unicode line-break opportunities, not existing newline characters. Contrast it with matching actual line endings on fixed text.

title: Unicode grapheme boundaries
notes: \b{gcb} identifies boundaries of grapheme clusters. A base character plus combining mark can form one cluster while length counts two characters.

title: resetting the start of a regex match
notes: \K keeps the consumed prefix outside the reported match and replacement. Use it to replace a suffix without capturing and reinserting its prefix.

title: possessive regex quantifiers
notes: Quantifiers such as ++ and *+ never give matched characters back. Contrast success and failure with greedy quantifiers; do not claim they are always faster or equivalent.

title: recursive regular expression subpatterns
notes: (?1) reuses capture group 1 as a subpattern and supports recursion for small balanced structures. Use bounded fixed inputs and anchor the complete pattern.

title: relative regular expression backreferences
notes: \g{-1} refers to the most recently opened capturing group. It can keep embedded patterns independent of earlier capture numbers.

title: generic linebreak matching
notes: \R matches Unicode linebreaks and treats CRLF as one sequence. Demonstrate splitting fixed mixed line endings rather than reading external files.

title: horizontal and vertical whitespace classes
notes: \h and \v distinguish horizontal and vertical whitespace; \H and \V are complements. Use fixed text to preserve line breaks while normalizing horizontal gaps.

title: resetting embedded regex modifiers
notes: (?^:...) resets the usual imsx flags and character-set mode to defaults for a group. Explicitly state which surrounding flag is being overridden.

title: ASCII-restricted regular expressions
notes: /a restricts \d, \s, \w and POSIX classes to ASCII. /aa additionally prevents ASCII/non-ASCII caseless matches; /a alone does not.

title: lexical regular expression defaults
notes: use re '/x' applies a regex flag within its lexical scope. The flags are chosen when the pattern is compiled, not globally for every future match.

title: explicit byte order in binary templates
notes: > and < modifiers select big- or little-endian order for supported pack/unpack template types. Use fixed-width templates and show bytes as hex, not raw binary.

title: temporarily deleting hash entries
notes: delete local $hash{key} hides an entry until scope exit, restoring its previous existence and value. Distinguish an absent key from a key holding undef.

title: keys values and each on arrays
notes: keys, values and each accept arrays. each @array yields an index and value in list context and maintains an iterator; do not mutate the array during iteration.

title: versions in package declarations
notes: package Name VERSION sets the package version at compile time from a literal. It does not load a module or set the required Perl interpreter version.

title: scoped package declarations
notes: package Name { ... } limits the package declaration to a block. Symbols remain package symbols rather than becoming lexically private.

title: automatic named character loading
notes: \N{FULL CHARACTER NAME} automatically loads the standard character-name support without use charnames. This does not enable UTF-8 source or output encoding.

title: C3 method resolution order
notes: use mro 'c3' selects C3 linearization for a package. Use a deterministic diamond hierarchy and inspect mro::get_linear_isa; the default remains depth-first search.

title: UNITCHECK compilation hooks
notes: UNITCHECK runs just after its compilation unit finishes compiling, unlike CHECK at the main compilation/execution transition. Use a self-contained program with fixed messages and no external loading.

title: fc
notes: Unicode case folding for caseless comparisons, not merely lowercasing.

title: unicode_eval
notes: String eval interprets characters consistently; does not enable UTF-8 source or make eval safe.

title: evalbytes
notes: Evaluates a byte string as Perl; never evaluate untrusted input.

title: __SUB__
notes: __SUB__ refers to the current subroutine, allowing anonymous recursion.

title: lexical subroutines
notes: Lexically scoped subroutine names; stable and always available since 5.26.

title: bitwise
notes: Numeric bitwise operators and dotted string variants; stable since 5.28.

title: isa
notes: Infix object class test; stable since 5.36.

title: nondestructive substitution
notes: The /r substitution modifier returns the modified string and preserves the original; it does not return a replacement count.

title: named regular expression captures
notes: (?<name>...) names a capture; $+{name} accesses it after a successful match.

title: regular expression noncapturing mode
notes: The /n modifier makes ordinary parentheses noncapturing; explicitly named groups still capture.

title: extended regular expressions with /xx
notes: /xx extends /x by ignoring unescaped spaces and tabs inside bracketed character classes. Escape literal spaces.
